**Bangla Voice Clock** (বাংলা ভয়েস ক্লক) now comes with proper installers for macOS and Windows.

## New

- **Installers.** A disk image for macOS (drag the app onto Applications) and a setup program for Windows. The Windows setup needs no administrator rights, adds a Start menu entry and an uninstaller, and starts the clock when you sign in (a box you can untick).
- **Quiet hours to the minute**, such as রাত ১১:৩০ to সকাল ৬:৪৫. The time picker shows the hours and the minutes side by side instead of one long list.
- On Windows, opening the app while it already runs shows the running clock instead of starting a second one.

## Fixed

- Between 12:00 and 12:59 the AI voice cut "বেজে" short ("দুপুর বারোটা বেজে …"). A handful of other openings lost a little of their last sound too; all are whole again.
- Thirty is now said "তিরিশ", which sounds fuller than the clipped "ত্রিশ".

## Download

| | |
|---|---|
| **macOS** 12 or later | `BanglaVoiceClock-v0.2.0-macos.dmg`: open it and drag **Bangla Voice Clock** onto **Applications**. It isn't signed yet: the first time, if macOS won't open it, go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and choose **Open Anyway** (on older macOS, right-click the app and choose **Open**). |
| **Windows** 10 or later (64-bit) | `BanglaVoiceClock-v0.2.0-windows-setup.exe`: run it and follow the two steps. SmartScreen may warn about an unknown publisher: choose **More info → Run anyway**. The clock then lives in the system tray (click the icon for the menu). Prefer no installer? `BanglaVoiceClock-v0.2.0-windows-portable.zip` runs from any folder. |

Settings from 0.1 carry over; quiet hours keep their whole-hour times until you change them.

## Known limits

- Builds are not code-signed yet.
- The Windows version has had less real-world use than the Mac version; please report anything odd.
- The classic voice only knows the quarter hours, as in 1998.
